page: Amazon Web Services g6.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. Compute capacity is delivered via an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 768 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, 7520 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and eight NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs providing a cumulative 179 GB of GPU VRAM. Networking throughput reaches a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations show exceptional parallel processing and accelerated throughput across multiple domains. Multi-core performance is firmly top tier, demonstrated by a stress-ng score of 286,988.18 and a PassMark CPU score of 109,870.16. GPU acceleration produces a top-tier Geekbench ray tracing score of 137,807.0 alongside strong LLM inference metrics, delivering 2,812.24 prompt tokens per second and 53.57 generation tokens per second on medium 7B models. In-memory operations also place in the top tier, with Redis SET achieving 159.29 million operations per second, supported by a large-block read memory bandwidth of 254.22 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center on the balance between specialized acceleration and single-threaded operations. While single-core performance scores remain in the strong tier at 2,989.99 in stress-ng and 1,686.0 in Geekbench, text decompression and processing metrics are closer to average cloud baselines. Cost efficiency is optimized for parallel architectures that can saturate the combination of 8 discrete L4 GPUs, high vCPU density, and local NVMe storage simultaneously.

The AWS g6.48xlarge is suited for machine learning inference pipelines, multi-stream video processing, real-time graphics rendering, large-scale Redis caching tiers, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial NVMe disk caching alongside dense GPU computing.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for intensive graphics and machine learning workloads. Powered by a 96-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processor delivering 192 vCPUs at 3.4 GHz, it incorporates 768 GB of DDR4 memory, 7520 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 100 Gbps baseline networking. Acceleration is driven by eight NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs equipped with 179 GB of aggregate VRAM. Benchmark results position the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute, Geekbench ray tracing, and Redis throughput at 159.29 million operations per second. LLM inference shows rapid prompt processing and text generation across small to large models. The platform offers strong resource density for parallel tasks, though single-threaded string processing remains average. It is well matched for machine learning inference, ray-traced rendering, high-throughput caching, and high-concurrency video processing pipelines.
